sentences.text: The single known specimen is nearly complete with mostly uncrushed bones that were not split during slab separation.
Yixianornis was about the size of a chicken, measuring 19 to 20 cm in length, 11.5 cm in height at the hips, and had a wingspan of about 40 cm.
The estimated body weight of Yixianornis was between 200 and 350 grams.
While Yixianornis had small peg-like teeth, the jaw tips were toothless and pockmarked with pits and grooves, possibly indicating a beak.
The breastbone had a strong keel for flight muscles and a unique fenestra found in yanornithiformes.
The fossil shows a backward-pointing hallux, but lacks clear evidence of the bone twist required for a permanently reversed toe.
Each wing had about five primary feathers, with the longest measuring approximately 6.7 cm.
This specimen is one of the few Mesozoic ornithurans preserving clear impressions of wing and tail feathers.
Carbonized tissue impressions reveal a rectrical bulb that allowed the tail feathers to fan out during flight and retract at rest.
The genus Yixianornis was described by Zhou and Zhang in 2001.
The species name grabaui honors American paleontologist Amadeus William Grabau.
A 2006 study suggests Yixianornis likely preferred dense vegetation environments due to its ability to fan its tail and broad wings for high maneuverability.
Yixianornis belongs to the parent group Hongshanornithidae.
Fossils of Yixianornis were found in the Jiufotang Formation near Chaoyang, China, dating to the early Aptian age approximately 120 million years ago.
The time range for Yixianornis is the Aptian stage, from 121.4 to 113.2 million years ago.
